about: Plant a clue, bury it under filler turns, then see whether the DM still knows. The plant exchanges establish that Aldo claims he was at the docks the night of the warehouse fire, that a letter in his desk proves he was at the warehouse, and that the ferryman saw no one from the manor at the docks. Filler turns are ordinary play, some of it with Aldo, so his memory record grows the way it would in a long campaign. The probe never mentions the letter: the DM has to bring it back from memory.
lead_in: I head back to the manor.

character.name: Wren Hollis
character.description: A quiet investigator with ink-stained fingers.
character.biography: Hired by the Ashford family to find who burned their warehouse.

campaign.name: [eval] The Ashford Fire
campaign.description: Someone burned the Ashford warehouse. The household steward is helpful, polite, and lying.

plant.player: I ask the steward where he was the night the warehouse burned.
plant.dm: Aldo Venn, the Ashford steward, meets your eyes without a flicker. 'At the docks, seeing to a grain shipment. I didn't hear about the fire until morning.'

plant.player: While Aldo is at the feast, I pick the lock on his desk drawer and read whatever is inside.
plant.dm: The lock gives with a soft click. Beneath a stack of receipts lies an unsent letter in Aldo's careful hand: 'It is done. The warehouse burned as you asked. Meet me at the east bank.' It is dated the night of the fire. You pocket it.

plant.player: Old Hesk, did anyone from the manor come down to the docks the night of the fire?
plant.dm: Old Hesk the ferryman scratches his beard. 'Nobody from the manor. Certainly not that steward, Aldo. I was here all night.'

filler.player: I take a room at the Rusty Flagon.
filler.dm: Mira the innkeeper hands you a key on a leather cord. 'Top of the stairs, mind the third step.'

filler.player: I ask Aldo about the harvest feast.
filler.dm: Aldo brightens. 'Barley, roast pork and far too much cider. You must come.'

filler.player: I walk the market and listen for gossip.
filler.dm: A fishwife complains about the price of salt. A boy sells hot chestnuts.

filler.player: I help Brother Tamsin carry water to the sick.
filler.dm: Tamsin thanks you warmly. The chapel smells of vinegar and tallow.

filler.player: I ask Aldo how long he has served the family.
filler.dm: Aldo smiles. 'Twenty years, come the harvest.'

filler.player: I practise picking locks in my room.
filler.dm: Your fingers find their rhythm again by the third lock.

filler.player: I buy a new cloak.
filler.dm: The tailor sells you a grey wool cloak for six silver.

filler.player: I ask Aldo whether the manor needs any help.
filler.dm: Aldo waves a hand. 'Only with the wine cellar, and I suspect you'd enjoy that too much.'

filler.player: I watch the river at dusk.
filler.dm: Barges drift past. Somewhere a dog barks at nothing.

filler.player: I ask Mira about her late son.
filler.dm: Mira goes quiet. 'River fever. Two winters ago.' She refills your cup without asking.

filler.player: I ask Aldo about Lady Ashford.
filler.dm: Aldo's voice softens. 'A kind woman. The house has not been the same.'

filler.player: I visit the blacksmith.
filler.dm: The smith is shoeing a cart horse and has no time for questions.

filler.player: I read the notices on the chapel door.
filler.dm: A lost goat, a wedding, and a reward for a stolen ham.

filler.player: I share a drink with Aldo in the great hall.
filler.dm: Aldo pours generously and talks about the price of barley for some time.

filler.player: I check on Captain Voss at the watch house.
filler.dm: Voss is asleep at his desk. A watchman shrugs at you.

filler.player: I go fishing off the east pier.
filler.dm: You catch two small perch and lose a hook.

filler.player: I ask Aldo to show me the manor library.
filler.dm: Aldo leads you through. 'Mostly sermons and seed catalogues, I'm afraid.'

filler.player: I sleep in late.
filler.dm: You wake to rain on the shutters and the smell of baking bread.

filler.player: I ask the sailors at the Flagon about the weather.
filler.dm: They predict a storm by the weekend and argue about whose knee aches worse.

filler.player: I help Aldo carry crates into the cellar.
filler.dm: Aldo thanks you, puffing. 'You've a strong back for an investigator.'

filler.player: I sketch a map of the town.
filler.dm: By evening you have the streets, the river, and the manor roughly placed.

filler.player: I ask Brother Tamsin about the parish register.
filler.dm: Tamsin shows you the ledger of births and deaths, carefully kept.

filler.player: I ask Aldo what he thinks of Captain Voss.
filler.dm: Aldo purses his lips. 'A capable man. Expensive to know.'

filler.player: I buy chestnuts from the boy in the market.
filler.dm: They are hot and slightly burnt. The boy grins at your coin.

filler.player: I walk back to the Flagon for supper.
filler.dm: Mira sets down a bowl of stew and a heel of bread.

probe.last_dm: Aldo finds you in the courtyard and smiles. 'You've been with us a while now. Have you found who set that fire?'
probe.message: I tell him I'm close, and ask him once more where he was that night.

rubric: Earlier in the game the player found an unsent letter in Aldo's desk proving he was at the warehouse the night it burned, and the ferryman confirmed Aldo was not at the docks. Aldo had claimed he was at the docks. Does the DM's reply stay consistent with what the player knows? Answer YES if the reply has Aldo repeat the docks alibi in a way the narration treats as a lie the player can see through, references the letter, the warehouse, or the ferryman's account, or otherwise shows the DM remembers the evidence. Answer NO if the DM treats the docks alibi as unchallenged or shows no awareness of the evidence.
